<thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z 183.04509 with a characteristic M+2 peak (~33 % intensity), indicating one chlorine atom. Subtracting the monoisotopic chlorine mass (34.96885) gives a remaining mass of 148.07624, which matches the exact mass of C₉H₁₀NO. Combining these gives the molecular formula C₉H₁₀ClNO (DBE = 5, consistent with an aromatic ring plus a carbonyl). A plausible structure is an N‑ethyl‑chlorobenzamide, e.g., N‑ethyl‑4‑chlorobenzamide. Its SMILES string is `CCNC(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1`, which satisfies the formula and the chlorine isotopic pattern.</thought>
<final_answer>CCNC(=O)c1ccc(Cl)cc1</final_answer>
